statements.action_statement: No fixed release is available yet; update when Docker Hardened Images publishes one.
statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-44842: libyaml 0.2.5 and earlier put no limit on how deeply YAML collections can nest. Each nesting level grows the parser's stacks and the number of earlier start events it has to check, so deeply nested input can exhaust the resources of a program that parses it. libyaml 0.2.6 fixes this with a configurable nesting depth limit, default 1000, set and read with yaml_set_max_nest_level() and yaml_get_max_nest_level(); in the released code the scanner enforces it and fails with "exceeded maximum nesting depth" (release notes: https://github.com/yaml/libyaml/releases/tag/0.2.6; first commit of the change: https://github.com/yaml/libyaml/commit/51843fe48257c6b7b6e70cdec1db634f64a40818). Debian lists trixie's libyaml 0.2.5-2 as vulnerable and only unstable's 0.2.6-1 as fixed (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-44842). This owner currently publishes one build, built from Debian's libyaml 0.2.5-2 with no added patches (its changelog lists only a rebuild). We downloaded every package of that build, libyaml-0-2, libyaml-dev and libyaml-0-2-dbgsym, for amd64 and arm64, and checked each against the repository checksum. None of libyaml-0.so.2.0.9, the static libyaml.a, the yaml.h header or the decompressed debug symbols contains yaml_set_max_nest_level, yaml_get_max_nest_level, MAX_NESTING_LEVEL or the "exceeded maximum nesting depth" error, while all of them name yaml_parser_parse. Every published build is therefore affected; no fixed build is published yet.
